The invention relates, in particular, to a device (3) for inspecting and measuring welding defects in a cylindrical wall (140), such as the wall (140) of a “vessel bottom penetration” (14) of a nuclear reactor. The device comprises an inspection head (4) forming a probe, which has a proximal end (EP) and a distal end (ED) along its longitudinal axis (X–X′) and includes a first side (42), referred to as the “inner” side, provided with at least one ultrasonic-wave transducer. - the wave transducer comprises an array (5) of adjacent elements (50), each element (50) serving as both an emitter and a receiver, the array (5) having a curved surface in the form of a cylindrical segment extending in the same direction as the longitudinal axis (X–X′) and having an outward-facing concavity; and

The invention is directed in particular to an apparatus (3) for detecting and assessing weld defects in a cylindrical wall (140), for example the wall (140) of a nuclear-reactor “vessel bottom penetration” (14). The apparatus includes an inspection head (4) serving as a probe. The head extends along a longitudinal axis (X–X′) between a proximal end (EP) and a distal end (ED) and has a first face (42), referred to as the “inner” face, equipped with at least one ultrasonic-wave transducer.

The apparatus is distinguished by the following features:

- Opposite the first face (42), the inspection head (4) has a second face (43), termed the “outer” face. This second face defines a curved surface corresponding to a portion of a cylinder, whose longitudinal axis is parallel to the head’s longitudinal axis (X–X′) and whose convex side faces outward.
- The ultrasonic-wave transducer is formed by an array (5) of adjoining elements (50), with every element (50) capable of both transmitting and receiving. The array (5) likewise defines a curved surface shaped as a cylindrical segment extending in the direction of the longitudinal axis (X–X′), but with its concave side facing outward.
- A plane (P1) passing through the two terminal generatrices of the cylindrical segment formed by the second face (43) is positioned at a non-zero acute angle β relative to a plane (P2) passing through the two terminal generatrices of the cylindrical segment formed by the transducer array (5).
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a device for detecting and measuring welding defects in cylindrical walls, particularly in vessel bottom penetrations used in nuclear reactors. The device comprises a probe-like control head extending along a longitudinal axis between a proximal end and a distal end.

The control head includes an inner side carrying at least one ultrasonic-wave transducer and an opposing outer side having a convex, partially cylindrical surface. The ultrasonic transducer is formed by a plurality of adjacent elements, each configured to operate both as an ultrasonic emitter and as a receiver. Together, these elements define a concave, partially cylindrical surface.

The geometry of the control head is such that the planes defined by the end generatrices of the convex outer surface and the concave transducer surface are inclined relative to one another. More specifically, these planes form a non-zero acute angle, enabling the device to be appropriately positioned for ultrasonic inspection and measurement of weld defects in cylindrical structures.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a probe-like ultrasonic inspection device for detecting, locating, and measuring defects in cylindrical walls, especially in the walls of penetrations extending through the bottom of a nuclear-reactor vessel. Such penetrations are difficult to inspect because of their limited accessibility, curved geometry, and the need to identify small cracks or other discontinuities reliably.

The device comprises a control head designed to be introduced into, or positioned against, the cylindrical wall to be examined. The head has two generally opposing curved surfaces. A first, outer surface is convex and is shaped to guide or support the head relative to the cylindrical geometry of the penetration. A second surface is concave and carries an ultrasonic transducer assembly. The transducer assembly includes a plurality of adjacent ultrasonic emitter-receiver elements arranged as an array, allowing ultrasonic waves to be transmitted into the wall and reflected signals to be received at multiple positions.

The convex outer surface and the concave surface supporting the ultrasonic array are oriented at an acute, nonzero angle relative to one another. This angular relationship directs the ultrasonic beams into the cylindrical wall along paths suited to detecting defects that might not be identifiable with a transducer positioned parallel or perpendicular to the wall. The angle also permits the array to maintain effective acoustic coupling while conforming to the restricted space and curvature of the penetration.

During inspection, the control head is moved axially and/or circumferentially relative to the cylindrical wall. The individual array elements may be activated separately or in selected groups to emit and receive ultrasonic signals. Reflections produced by cracks, lack of bonding, inclusions, wall thinning, or other discontinuities are recorded and analyzed. By comparing signals obtained from multiple elements and probe positions, the location, orientation, and dimensions of a defect can be determined.

The arrangement therefore provides reliable coverage of cylindrical components while reducing the need for numerous separate probes or complex repositioning operations. It is particularly suitable for nondestructive examination of nuclear-reactor vessel-bottom penetrations, although it may also be used for pipes, sleeves, nozzles, tubes, bores, and other components having cylindrical or substantially cylindrical walls.

### The Power of “The”

“The” is one of the most common words in the English language. Known as the definite article, it identifies a specific person, place, object, or idea. For example, “the book” refers to a particular book that the speaker and listener already know about.

Although it is short and simple, “the” plays an important role in communication. It adds clarity, creates emphasis, and helps distinguish something specific from something general. Without it, many English sentences would sound incomplete or unclear. This small word demonstrates how even the simplest parts of language can have a significant impact.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract describing an ultrasonic inspection device for detecting and measuring welding defects in the cylindrical wall of a nuclear reactor vessel bottom penetration.
counterfactuals.output: An ultrasonic inspection device is provided for detecting and measuring defects in a weld associated with a cylindrical bottom penetration of a nuclear reactor vessel. The device includes a probe carrier configured for insertion into, or positioning around, the cylindrical wall of the penetration and having a plurality of ultrasonic transducers oriented to direct ultrasonic beams through the wall toward the weld and adjacent heat-affected regions. A drive assembly produces controlled axial and circumferential movement of the probe carrier, while position sensors correlate received ultrasonic signals with inspection coordinates. The transducers may include phased-array elements operable at selected beam angles and focal depths to detect cracks, lack of fusion, porosity, and other discontinuities. A coupling system maintains acoustic transmission between the transducers and the cylindrical wall. A processor acquires and analyzes reflected ultrasonic signals to determine the location, orientation, depth, and extent of a detected defect and to generate a mapped representation of the inspected region. The device enables in situ, substantially complete volumetric inspection of the penetration weld with reduced reactor-vessel access requirements.

The head (4) carries at least one translator array (5) comprising a plurality of individually controllable electroacoustic transducers arranged to transmit ultrasonic inspection signals into the wall (140) and to receive corresponding reflected signals therefrom. The translator array (5) is oriented such that respective ultrasonic beams intersect the weld at a plurality of incidence angles and inspection depths, thereby permitting volumetric examination of the weld and adjacent heat-affected regions. The head (4) further comprises a coupling arrangement configured to maintain acoustic coupling between the translator array (5) and the wall (140), and a positioning assembly configured to maintain a predetermined spacing and orientation of the translator array (5) relative to the cylindrical surface during circumferential and/or axial movement of the device (3). Signals received by the translator array (5) are processed to determine the presence, position, dimensions, and orientation of weld defects without impairing the structural integrity of the wall (140).
